subproblem.title: Quantitative right inverse on balls of a near-linear self-map of R^n
subproblem.statement: Let n be a natural number, Phi : R^n -> R^n a function, A : R^n -> R^n a continuous linear map, c in R^n, r > 0 and 0 <= eps <= 1/24. Assume (H1) |A h| >= (11/12)|h| for every h in R^n; (H2) |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2) - A(x1 - x2)| <= eps |x1 - x2| for all x1, x2 in the closed ball B_r(0); (H3) Phi(0) = c. Then there is X : R^n -> R^n such that (1) for every w in the closed ball B_{r/2}(c), X(w) lies in the closed ball B_{3r/5}(0) and Phi(X(w)) = w; (2) if x is in B_r(0), w is in B_{r/2}(c) and Phi(x) = w, then x = X(w); (3) (7/8)|X(w1) - X(w2)| <= |w1 - w2| for all w1, w2 in B_{r/2}(c).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (Φ : Rn n → Rn n) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn n) (c : Rn n) (r ε : ℝ), 0 < r → 0 ≤ ε → ε ≤ 1 / 24 → (∀ h : Rn n, 11 / 12 * ‖h‖ ≤ ‖A h‖) → (∀ x₁ ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, ∀ x₂ ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, ‖Φ x₁ - Φ x₂ - A (x₁ - x₂)‖ ≤ ε * ‖x₁ - x₂‖) → Φ 0 = c → ∃ X : Rn n → Rn n, (∀ w ∈ closedBall c (r / 2), X w ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) (3 * r / 5) ∧ Φ (X w) = w) ∧ (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, ∀ w ∈ closedBall c (r / 2), Φ x = w → x = X w) ∧ (∀ w₁ ∈ closedBall c (r / 2), ∀ w₂ ∈ closedBall c (r / 2), 7 / 8 * ‖X w₁ - X w₂‖ ≤ ‖w₁ - w₂‖)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: B_s(p) is the closed ball {x : |x - p| <= s} of R^n and |.| the Euclidean norm. Hypotheses: (H1) |A h| >= (11/12)|h| for all h; (H2) |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2) - A(x1 - x2)| <= eps |x1 - x2| for x1, x2 in B_r(0); (H3) Phi(0) = c; moreover r > 0 and 0 <= eps <= 1/24.
Provenance: steps 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 below are steps 4, 2, 5, 7 and 9 of the parent regraph proof, specialised to an abstract map Phi; every step is proved in full here and nothing from the parent is assumed.
1. Injectivity estimate. Let x1, x2 be in B_r(0). By the triangle inequality, |A(x1 - x2)| <= |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2)| + |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2) - A(x1 - x2)|. By (H1) the left side is >= (11/12)|x1 - x2|, and by (H2) the last term is <= eps|x1 - x2| <= (1/24)|x1 - x2|. Hence |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2)| >= (11/12 - 1/24)|x1 - x2| = (7/8)|x1 - x2|.
2. Invertibility of A. If A a = A b, then (H1) gives (11/12)|a - b| <= |A(a - b)| = 0, so a = b: A is injective. An injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space R^n is surjective (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective), so A is bijective; let A^{-1} be its inverse, which is linear. For k in R^n, (H1) with h = A^{-1} k gives (11/12)|A^{-1} k| <= |A(A^{-1} k)| = |k|, i.e. |A^{-1} k| <= (12/11)|k|.
3. Solving Phi(x) = w. Claim: for every w in B_{r/2}(c) there is x in B_{3r/5}(0) with Phi(x) = w.
Put g(x) := Phi(x) - c - A x. By (H3) and A 0 = 0, g(0) = 0. For x1, x2 in B_r(0), g(x1) - g(x2) = Phi(x1) - Phi(x2) - A(x1 - x2), so (H2) gives |g(x1) - g(x2)| <= eps|x1 - x2|; with x2 = 0 this gives |g(x)| <= eps|x| for x in B_r(0).
Let K := B_{3r/5}(0). Since 3r/5 <= r, K is contained in B_r(0); K is a nonempty closed subset of the complete space R^n, hence complete. Fix w in B_{r/2}(c) and define F_w(x) := A^{-1}(w - c - g(x)).
- F_w maps K into K: for x in K, |F_w(x)| <= (12/11)(|w - c| + |g(x)|) <= (12/11)(r/2 + eps * 3r/5) <= (12/11)(r/2 + r/40) = 63r/110 < 66r/110 = 3r/5.
- F_w is a contraction of K: for x1, x2 in K, linearity of A^{-1} gives F_w(x1) - F_w(x2) = A^{-1}(g(x2) - g(x1)), so |F_w(x1) - F_w(x2)| <= (12/11) eps |x1 - x2| <= (12/11)(1/24)|x1 - x2| = (1/22)|x1 - x2|.
By the Banach fixed point theorem F_w has a fixed point x in K. Then A x = w - c - g(x), i.e. Phi(x) = c + A x + g(x) = w. This proves the claim.
[Lean: ContractingWith is not imported by GMT.Ch05.Submission. The in-scope lemma ApproximatesLinearOn.surjOn_closedBall_of_nonlinearRightInverse (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/ApproximatesLinearOn.lean:143) packages exactly this argument. (H2) is literally ApproximatesLinearOn Phi A (closedBall 0 r) <eps, 0 <= eps> (constant as an NNReal). Step 2 provides a ContinuousLinearMap.NonlinearRightInverse of A with toFun := Function.surjInv (surjectivity of A), nnnorm := 12/11, bound' from (H1) as in step 2, and right_inv' := Function.surjInv_eq. With centre 0 and radius 3r/5 (closedBall 0 (3r/5) is contained in closedBall 0 r) the lemma gives SurjOn Phi (closedBall 0 (3r/5)) (closedBall (Phi 0) (((12/11)^{-1} - eps) * (3r/5))). Since Phi 0 = c and (11/12 - eps)(3r/5) >= (11/12 - 1/24)(3r/5) = 21r/40 >= r/2, this target ball contains B_{r/2}(c).]
4. Definition of X; conclusion (1). For w in B_{r/2}(c) let X(w) be a point x of B_{3r/5}(0) with Phi(x) = w, chosen by step 3 (choice); for w not in B_{r/2}(c) put X(w) := 0. Then (1) holds. In particular X(w) is in B_{3r/5}(0), which is contained in B_r(0), for every w in B_{r/2}(c).
5. Conclusion (2). Let x be in B_r(0) and w in B_{r/2}(c) with Phi(x) = w. By step 4, X(w) is in B_r(0) and Phi(X(w)) = w. Step 1 gives (7/8)|x - X(w)| <= |Phi(x) - Phi(X(w))| = |w - w| = 0, hence x = X(w).
6. Conclusion (3). For w1, w2 in B_{r/2}(c), step 4 gives X(w1), X(w2) in B_r(0) with Phi(X(w1)) = w1 and Phi(X(w2)) = w2, so step 1 gives (7/8)|X(w1) - X(w2)| <= |Phi(X(w1)) - Phi(X(w2))| = |w1 - w2|.
proof_key_steps: Injectivity estimate: |Phi x1 - Phi x2| >= (11/12 - eps)|x1 - x2| >= (7/8)|x1 - x2| on B_r(0) from (H1), (H2) and eps <= 1/24
A injective, hence bijective in finite dimension, with |A^{-1} k| <= (12/11)|k|

Contraction F_w(x) = A^{-1}(w - c - g(x)) on B_{3r/5}(0) (Lean: ApproximatesLinearOn.surjOn_closedBall_of_nonlinearRightInverse with nnnorm 12/11) gives B_{r/2}(c) inside Phi(B_{3r/5}(0)) since (11/12 - 1/24)(3r/5) = 21r/40 >= r/2
Choose X(w) for w in B_{r/2}(c) (else 0); uniqueness (2) and the 8/7-Lipschitz bound (3) follow from the injectivity estimate

subproblem.title: The graph map x -> y + q(graphPoint x (v x)) is C^1 with derivative h -> q(graphPoint h (Dv(x) h))
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, q a linear isometric equivalence of R^{n+l}, v : R^n -> R^l, y in R^{n+l} and U an open subset of R^n. If v is C^1 on U, then Psi(x) := y + q(graphPoint x (v x)) is C^1 on U, and for every x in U and h in R^n, fderiv Psi x h = q(graphPoint h (fderiv v x h)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (U : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 v U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun x => y + q (graphPoint x (v x))) U ∧ ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ h : Rn n, fderiv ℝ (fun x => y + q (graphPoint x (v x))) x h = q (graphPoint h (fderiv ℝ v x h))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : R^{n+l} -> R^n x R^l, Mathlib's canonical continuous linear equivalence (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean:378) sending z to the pair (first n coordinates of z, last l coordinates of z), i.e. (E z).1 i = z(Fin.castAdd l i) and (E z).2 j = z(Fin.natAdd n j). Let Psi(x) := y + q(graphPoint x (v x)). Hypotheses: q is a linear isometric equivalence of R^{n+l}, U is open and v is C^1 on U.
Provenance: this is the chain-rule computation in step 8 of the parent regraph proof, together with its coordinate identity (i), which is proved here in step 1 because the parent's sibling lemma is not available to this node; nothing from the parent is assumed.
1. graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b) for all a in R^n and b in R^l. By definition graphPoint a b is the vector of R^{n+l} with coordinates Fin.append a b; its Fin.castAdd l i-th coordinate is a i and its Fin.natAdd n j-th coordinate is b j (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). Hence E(graphPoint a b) = (a, b) componentwise, and applying E^{-1} proves the claim. [Lean: apply E.injective; rw [ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]; ext i <;> simp [graphPoint].]
2. Put L := q o E^{-1}, a continuous linear map R^n x R^l -> R^{n+l} (q is a linear isometry, hence continuous linear, and E^{-1} is continuous linear). By step 1, L(a, b) = q(graphPoint a b) for all a, b; hence Psi(x) = y + L(x, v x) for every x in R^n.
3. Psi is C^1 on U. The map x -> (x, v x) is C^1 on U because both components are: the identity is C^infinity and v is C^1 on U (ContDiffOn.prodMk). Composing with the continuous linear map L, which is C^infinity (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff.comp_contDiffOn), and adding the constant y (contDiffOn_const.add) preserves C^1 on U. By step 2 the resulting map is Psi.
4. The derivative. Fix x in U. Since U is open and v is C^1 on U with 1 != 0, v is differentiable at x, i.e. v has derivative Dv := fderiv v x at x. Hence x' -> (x', v x') has derivative h -> (h, Dv h) at x (HasFDerivAt.prodMk of hasFDerivAt_id and the derivative of v). A continuous linear map is its own derivative, so by the chain rule x' -> L(x', v x') has derivative h -> L(h, Dv h) at x, and adding the constant y does not change the derivative (HasFDerivAt.const_add). Therefore fderiv Psi x is the map h -> L(h, Dv h), and by step 2, fderiv Psi x h = q(graphPoint h (fderiv v x h)) for every h in R^n.
proof_key_steps: graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b) for E = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd, checked coordinatewise via Fin.append
Psi(x) = y + L(x, v x) with L := q o E^{-1} continuous linear
C^1 on U: compose the C^1 map x -> (x, v x) with L and add the constant y
Chain rule at x in U: Psi has derivative h -> L(h, Dv(x) h) = q(graphPoint h (fderiv v x h))

subproblem.title: C^1 regularity and derivative bound for a continuous right inverse of a C^1 map
subproblem.statement: Let n be a natural number, Phi, X : R^n -> R^n functions, U, W subsets of R^n and kappa a real number. Assume U and W are open, kappa > 0, Phi is C^1 on U, kappa |h| <= |fderiv Phi x h| for every x in U and h in R^n, X is continuous on W, and for every w in W, X(w) is in U and Phi(X(w)) = w. Then X is C^1 on W and the operator norm of fderiv X w is at most 1/kappa for every w in W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (Φ X : Rn n → Rn n) (U W : Set (Rn n)) (κ : ℝ), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → 0 < κ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ U → (∀ x ∈ U, ∀ h : Rn n, κ * ‖h‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ Φ x h‖) → ContinuousOn X W → (∀ w ∈ W, X w ∈ U ∧ Φ (X w) = w) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 X W ∧ ∀ w ∈ W, ‖fderiv ℝ X w‖ ≤ κ⁻¹
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: for x in U write DPhi(x) := fderiv Phi x, a continuous linear endomorphism of R^n; norms of linear maps are operator norms. End := (R^n ->L[R] R^n), the continuous linear endomorphisms of R^n, is a complete normed ring (R^n is finite-dimensional, hence complete). Hypotheses: U and W are open; kappa > 0; (H1) Phi is C^1 on U; (H2) kappa|h| <= |DPhi(x) h| for all x in U and h in R^n; (H3) X is continuous on W; (H4) X(w) is in U and Phi(X(w)) = w for every w in W.
Provenance: this is the abstract form of steps 8, 10 and 11 of the parent regraph proof (invertibility of the chart derivative, the local-left-inverse rule, continuity of the inverse derivative); every step is proved in full here and nothing from the parent is assumed.
1. Each DPhi(x), x in U, is invertible with |DPhi(x)^{-1}| <= 1/kappa. Fix x in U and let L := DPhi(x). If L a = L b, then (H2) gives kappa|a - b| <= |L(a - b)| = 0, and kappa > 0 gives a = b. So L is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space R^n, hence bijective (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FiniteDimensional/Basic.lean:412). Linear maps between finite-dimensional normed spaces are continuous, so L is the forward map of a continuous linear equivalence L~ of R^n (LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv). For k in R^n, (H2) at h = L~^{-1} k gives kappa|L~^{-1} k| <= |L(L~^{-1} k)| = |k|, so |L~^{-1} k| <= kappa^{-1}|k|; by ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound (with 0 <= kappa^{-1}), |L~^{-1}| <= kappa^{-1}.
2. Regularity of Phi on U. Let x be in U. The open set U is a neighbourhood of x, and Phi is C^1 on U with 1 != 0, so Phi is differentiable at x: Phi has derivative DPhi(x) at x. Moreover x -> DPhi(x) is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Defs.lean:916, using 1 <= 1).
3. Derivative of X and the bound. Fix w in W, put x0 := X(w), which lies in U by (H4), and let L~ be the equivalence of step 1 at x0. Three facts hold:
- X is continuous at w, because X is continuous on W (H3) and the open set W is a neighbourhood of w;
- Phi has derivative L~ = DPhi(x0) at X(w) (step 2);
- Phi(X(w')) = w' for all w' in the neighbourhood W of w (H4).
By the local-left-inverse rule (HasFDerivAt.of_local_left_inverse, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/OfCompLeft.lean:165), X has derivative L~^{-1} at w. Consequently X is differentiable at every point of W, fderiv X w = L~^{-1}, and |fderiv X w| <= kappa^{-1} by step 1. This is the second conclusion.
4. The derivative of X through the ring inverse. With w, x0 and L~ as in step 3, DPhi(x0) is the underlying element of the unit u := L~.toUnit of End (ContinuousLinearEquiv.toUnit), and the inverse of u is L~^{-1}. Hence Ring.inverse(DPhi(X(w))) = (u^{-1} : End) = L~^{-1} = fderiv X w (Ring.inverse_unit). So fderiv X w = Ring.inverse(DPhi(X(w))) for every w in W.
5. Continuity of fderiv X on W. Fix w in W and put x0 := X(w), which is in U.
- w' -> DPhi(X(w')) is continuous at w: X is continuous at w (step 3), and DPhi is continuous at x0 since it is continuous on the open set U containing x0 (step 2).
- Ring.inverse is continuous at every unit of the complete normed ring End (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt, Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Units.lean:183), in particular at DPhi(x0), which is the unit L~.toUnit of step 4.
- Hence w' -> Ring.inverse(DPhi(X(w'))) is continuous at w. By step 4 it agrees with fderiv X on the neighbourhood W of w, so fderiv X is continuous at w.
Thus fderiv X is continuous on W. [Alternative estimate: if P := DPhi(X(w')) and Q := DPhi(X(w)) with inverses P~^{-1}, Q~^{-1} from step 1, then P~^{-1} - Q~^{-1} = P~^{-1}(Q - P)Q~^{-1}, so |P~^{-1} - Q~^{-1}| <= kappa^{-2}|P - Q|, which tends to 0 as w' -> w by the first bullet.]
6. X is C^1 on W. W is open, X is differentiable on W (step 3) and fderiv X is continuous on W (step 5). By contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Defs.lean:891) applied with 1 = 0 + 1 (its middle condition, 0 = top in WithTop ENat (i.e. order omega) -> AnalyticOn, is vacuous because 0 != top), together with contDiffOn_zero (C^0 on W is continuity on W), X is C^1 on W. [Equivalently, at each w in W use contDiffAt_succ_iff_hasFDerivAt (Defs.lean:1018) with n = 0 and contDiffAt_zero (Defs.lean:1129), whose neighbourhood is W.] This is the first conclusion.
proof_key_steps: For x in U, DPhi(x) is injective by the lower bound, hence (finite dimension) a continuous linear equivalence with |DPhi(x)^{-1}| <= 1/kappa
Phi is differentiable on the open set U and fderiv Phi is continuous on U
Local-left-inverse rule (HasFDerivAt.of_local_left_inverse): X has derivative DPhi(X w)^{-1} at each w in W, so |fderiv X w| <= 1/kappa
fderiv X w = Ring.inverse(DPhi(X w)); continuity of X, of fderiv Phi and of Ring.inverse at units gives continuity of fderiv X on W
Differentiable with continuous derivative on the open set W implies C^1 on W (contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen, contDiffOn_zero)

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose, including openness, positive κ, continuity of X and its right-inverse property. The lower derivative bound gives an invertible endomorphism and inverse norm at most κ⁻¹. The local-left-inverse lemma has exactly the required orientation and hypotheses. Openness justifies continuity at points and neighborhood identities; continuity of ring inversion then gives a continuous derivative on W, establishing C¹ regularity. Ring.inverse uses the ordinary continuous-linear-endomorphism ring. The argument is complete and non-circular.
